title: Walter Page, Joe Keyes and Ben Webster try to keep him in the band
summary: Page, Ben Webster and Joe Keyes pressure him to join Basie, but he insists he can only play five or six pieces.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: Now who was in this? This was a band that Basie had gotten from Bennie Moten and from Walter Page, and Walter Page came to get you, is that right?
Walter asked me to go to play with him. Of course Mac Washinton was going to play with Benny at the Harlem Club on 15th-La Salle. Ben Webster, Walter Page, and Joe Keyes had me -
Joe Keyes was a great trumpet player.

Trumpet player. They had me in the washroom and wouldn't let me out and they were going down the street and they were stealing whiskey and they was keeping me in there and Ben Webster wanted to slap me. I said, "I can't play with that band!"
Was Ben in the band too?

No, Ben was with Andy Kirk but Ben was trying to get me to go with Basie. And I said, "No, I can't play with this band." That band had destroyed me, Milt. I said I can only play about 5 or 6 pieces; I can't play with that band.
